julia.peopleops: Hey team — quick one. Employee on unpaid parental LOA waived benefits at open enrollment (they opted out to avoid deductions). They’re returning to work 2024-07-15 and want health coverage to be effective retro to their LOA return date (so no gap). What’s the correct process for a midyear re-enroll after an LOA waiver? Any limits on backdating, proration, and how payroll handles missed deductions?
samuel.lee: Hi — standard flow: employee files a QLE (return from unpaid LOA) within 30 days of return. People Ops submits a benefits transaction to HRIS to add coverage with the requested effective date. HRIS can sometimes backdate depending on plan/carrier rules. We need the LOA approval doc and the signed QLE form.
julia.peopleops: got it. carrier flexibility w/ backdating is the main variable, right? if carrier allows retro, do we create a payroll catch-up to collect missed employee premiums?
samuel.lee: correct. Carriers: some accept retro enrollments up to 60 days from effective date, others only forward effective dates. If carrier accepts retro, benefits team marks the enrollment effective to 2024-07-15 and payroll posts a catch-up for employee-share premiums. If carrier doesn’t accept retro, we start coverage on the enrollment processing date and note the gap.
hris-bot: Automated note: HRIS transaction types for LOA-return QLE: `LOA_RETURN_REENROLL` (supports requested effective_date field). Max retro window: carrier-dependent; system limit for backdate requests = 60 days. Attach required documents: LOA approval memo, QLE form, ID verification if partner added.
payroll-bot: Payroll FYI — we can run a catch-up deduction in the next pay run if we receive `effective_date`, `benefit_code`, and `employee_premium_amount` before payroll cutoff (T-5 business days). For transparency: catch-up will be one-time additive deduction. Tax treatment: deductions are pre-tax for medical but check state rules for retro withholdings. Example journal line we need in the ticket body:```
benefit_code: MED_PREM
effective_date: 2024-07-15
employee_premium_amount: 124.50
payroll_action: one_time_catchup
```
anna.manager: confirming this employee (Maya Torres) returns 7/15 and intends to re-add spouse coverage. She signed LOA docs and QLE yesterday. I can attach to the ticket. :thumbsup:
julia.peopleops: thanks Anna. A couple follow-ups: 1) HSA: if they elected HSA at OE but waived deductions, can we retro deposit employer contribution and catch up payroll deductions into HSA? 2) FSA dependent care — any retro funding allowed?
samuel.lee: HSA — yes, we can do catch-up payroll contributions into HSA as long as plan year maximums aren’t exceeded. Employee must have been eligible for those months. Employer-side contributions can be posted retro if plan permits; we submit to vendor with `effective_date`. FSA — more restrictive: dependent care FSA cannot be retro-funded for prior pay periods. Health FSA sometimes allows midyear elections only via QLE but pre-funding depends on vendor. Recommend: confirm with carrier/vendor for both.
hris-bot: Reminder: When adding a dependent, include dependent DOB and documentation (marriage cert or domestic partnership affidavit). Uploads go to benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.example/portal (internal link).
julia.peopleops: ok will open the HRIS ticket. I'll include the LOA approval, signed QLE, dependent docs, and payroll journal snippet above. Sam — anything else about payroll proration vs catch-up?
samuel.lee: Two paths: (A) Prorate future deductions (spread missed premiums over remaining pay periods) — cleaner for employees, but requires payroll config to spread `one_time_catchup` as `spread_over_n_periods`. (B) Single catch-up deduction (one-time). Choose based on employee preference. Note: if employee wants to spread, we need to file before payroll cutoff for next cycle and specify `spread_periods`.
julia.peopleops: noted. I'll ask employee preference and submit ticket today. tagging @payroll-bot here so they see required fields.
payroll-bot: Received. Please create ticket with subject: "M. Torres LOA-return reenroll + payroll catch-up" and include: `employee_id`, `benefit_code`, `effective_date`, `employee_premium_amount`, `spread_periods` (if desired). We'll acknowledge within 1 business day.
anna.manager: thx all — i'll have Maya confirm spread vs one-time today.
julia.peopleops: perfect. I'll post updates in ticket. Closing Slack thread once processed. :white_check_mark:
